thread.title: Small rockets to create big impact on Florida's Space Coast

author: Matthew Richardson
title: Small rockets to create big impact on Florida's Space Coast
text: – Staff writer, Orlando Business Journal Jan 30, 2019, 5:16pm EST Watch out, SpaceX and United Launch Alliance: Smaller competitors may be coming for you. Several firms in the commercial space industry are laying the groundwork to make a big impact in Central Florida by launching smaller rockets as often as once a week or more for a fraction of the price to keep up with the growing demand from satellite companies. As technology advances and satellites become smaller and less expensive, companies can send devices to space more often, said Sid Gutierrez , chairman of Cocoa-based rocket maker and launch service company Rocket Crafters Inc. In fact, more than 1,000 small satellites were launched into space between 2012 and 2017, and six times as many were launched in 2017 when compared with 2012, according to Alexandria, Va.-based analytic consulting firm Bryce Space & Technology LLC. More launch activity on Florida’s Space Coast would attract more workers to the region, while also bringing more visitors to see the launches and provide traffic to existing businesses. And the demand is creating plenty more work for launch service providers. For example, Arlington, Va.-based OneWeb LLC wants to send 1,000-plus satellites into orbit from Florida. Of course, industry giants like Hawthorne, Calif.-based SpaceX and Centennial, Colo.-based ULA — a joint venture between Lockheed Martin Corp. (NYSE: LMT) and The Boeing Co. (NYSE: BA) — still will have those small satellites on board. But they often have to include many other devices in their payload to justify the use of such a large vehicle and to reduce the price with shared costs. Plus, big rocket launch schedules change often, since larger government clients take priority. “Customers need the right-sized rocket for a small-sized satellite,” Gutierrez said. Small rockets can keep up with the demand for a much cheaper price. SpaceX’s cost to launch its Falcon 9 rocket is $62 million, while Rocket Crafters will cost about $9 million per launch. Rocket Crafters plans to launch its Intrepid-1 rocket sometime in 2020 from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. But it’s not alone in eyeing Space Coast opportunities. Los Angeles-based 3-D rocket factory and launch services firm Relativity Space Inc. last month took its first step toward getting approval to use Cape Canaveral Air Force Station’s Launch Complex 16. Relativity Space claims it will deploy and resupply satellite constellations with an “industry-defining lead time and cost.” Additionally, an unnamed company wants to invest $52 million to create 239 jobs paying an average annual salary of $70,000 to use Space Launch Complex 20 at the Cape Canaveral Spaceport. All this activity will give Central Florida a bigger share of the growing global satellite industry, which reported 2017 revenue of $268.6 billion — up 3 percent from 2016, Washington, D.C.-based Satellite Industry Association’s most recent report showed. That’s why there “absolutely” is an opportunity for small companies to compete with the giants, according to Tom Stroup, president of the Satellite Industry Association. “Sometimes, with the larger rocket companies, you are one of 50 clients waiting to get your device in space, so your timing is not in your control.” Show me the money Orlando software startup secures large sum in VC funding A local company that creates software for its clients to better manage Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL) workplace products just landed a large chunk of venture capital funding. Orlando-based Mosyle Corp. on Jan. 28 got $16 million from Lehi, Utah-based Peak Ventures and New York-based Elephant Ventures. The funding will allow Mosyle to create and market its Mosyle Business platform, extending its services to a wide variety of companies and organizations that use mobile devices. This platform also gives a company’s IT department better access to a mobile device in case anything needs to be uploaded or fixed. Mosyle currently uses its manager platform as a mobile device management solution for public schools. The Mosyle Management platform allows schools to secure and enforce policies on smartphones and tablets, and it’s used by 8,500-plus schools in more than 70 countries. Ready for Liftoff SpaceX completes fire test, sets possible launch date for unmanned demo Hawthorne, Calif.-based SpaceX announced its next big Crew Dragon mission may launch from Florida’s Space Coast as early as Feb. 9 at 11 a.m. SpaceX originally had planned a Jan. 17 unmanned test launch for the Crew Dragon capsule — the one that eventually will take astronauts into space from U.S. soil for the first time since 2011. But the launch was delayed due, in part, to the federal government shutdown. SpaceX on Jan. 24 announced on Twitter that it completed a static fire test of its Falcon 9 rocket with the Crew Dragon on top at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A. The February test mission will be uncrewed, but a following one in June will use the capsule to take astronauts to the International Space Station. Ranked by C. Fla. employees Rank
